summary: A career-history interview conducted through comics rather than celebrity biography. David Choe reconstructs the Los Angeles shops, magazines, art-school influences, self-publishing, pornography illustration, graffiti, and chance editorial contacts that formed Slow Jams and his early career. The hosts’ detailed comics knowledge makes this unusually valuable for identifying works, collaborators, and chronology.

chapters.title: Los Angeles comics shops and growing up around the medium
Wizard, art school, and the origins of Slow Jams
Illustration work, writing, and Giant Robot
Money, scarcity, and making work available

connections.label: Slow Jams as the career hinge
connections.note: The episode ties the comic to Wizard coverage, Marvel interest, later collector prices, and Choe’s resistance to scarcity. It should be a first-class work page linking every later recollection.

connections.label: Los Angeles creative infrastructure
connections.note: Meltdown, Golden Apple, Giant Robot, Koreatown, graffiti walls, and adult-magazine offices appear as a local ecosystem rather than unrelated anecdotes. The archive should expose this as a place-based path.

connections.label: Dirty Hands as external memory
connections.note: The hosts refer to the documentary while questioning Choe’s account. This creates a useful evidence edge between present recollection, earlier documentary footage, and surviving publications.
